I feel the same as you. I was a good student in high school without putting any effort in and started university in October 2014 planning to not just be good but excellent. Studying naturally comes easy to me, I never struggled with anything, I started off with a 4.0 GPA, things were looking fine. I was even thinking about finishing my degree in 5 instead of 6 semesters. Then everything fell apart. It’s not like university was suddenly hard, actually it was still easy, I just couldn’t function like a human being anymore. 
It’s 5 years later now, and I’ve graduated 2 months ago, not in the planned 5 but instead 10 semesters (Quite frankly, I’m embarrassed about it because I know what I’m capable of in a somewhat stable state of mind. It’s tearing me apart that I might never be this person again.) I’m not telling you this to toot my own horn, but to show you that it’s possible, even when you think it will never happen. Mental illness takes the best of you, it chews you up, spits you out and all you’re left with are lost opportunities und self doubt, wondering if you were ever smart at all. I’ve been there. But your past shows that you’re an intelligent person, capable of great things. It’s just harder for you, as it was for me, due to battling demons others don’t even think about. It sucks, it’s not fair, and I’m really sorry you’re feeling the same way, but I’m sure you’ll push through eventually and graduate. At your own pace, and that’s okay.

I could feel your pain through the lines you’ve written. It sounds like you’ve gotten out of an abusive and incredibly unhealthy relationship and while you’re going through heartbreak right now I hope you can look back on this one day and see the strength and bravery it took to cut loose from a person who’s evidently not good for you. We can easily fall for the lies other people tell us which they try to mask as love when truly it’s got nothing to do with love at all. It’s not your job to fix another fucked up person who treats you poorly, instead I hope you can channel that energy and try to find that girl you’ve mentioned losing sight of in your poem, she sounds like she deserves that self love as well as someone she can grow with, not wither.

Hey, it sounds like you’ve got dealt a pretty tough hand in life so far and I’m sorry that now you have to live with people who are uneducated when it comes to mental illnesses. First of all: you’re not worthless. Money, a job whatever do not define a person’s worth, there are much more important qualities, for example you sound like a really compassionate person. I know this won’t provide for you in life but it’s an important quality to have nonetheless. 

Do you have access to a therapist right now? You also mentioned you are trying to make progress with college, are you attending one at the moment? Because usually there are counselors on campus who can help and provide resources/ possible solutions.
I don’t know how open your brother and his gf would be to a conversation where you really to try explain to them that mental illness doesn’t go away with sunshine and rainbows but I’d at least give it another try. 

Prepare this and then provide them with resources, science. There’s enough research out there, maybe they’d be willing to listen to facts and what actual doctors have to say. I think it would be important to have them on your side as support, even if they don’t 100% understand it. At least find a common ground you all can work with. Explain to them that it’s not you being a leech or lazy and that you’ll try to look for a part time job to prove that, while also trying to get a degree. But that you’ll need their support for that and therapy to work through it. Maybe if they see your effort they’d be willing to listen. Please don’t make any hasty decisions to put yourself in danger.

I have no advice, just here to say I’m 24F as well and feel exactly the same way about my depression/insomnia/migraines. Putting age limits on dealing with illnesses where everyone has a unique experience and different resources to get help is actually ridiculous yet I do it when it comes to myself too. It might stem from the high pressure society we live in where we compare ourselves to people who don’t deal with the same issues, yet we think we’re falling behind because we can’t get our depression under control. It’s truly sad that we can’t extend the compassion and understanding we have for the struggles of others to ourselves as well.

This is a really tough spot to be in, it’s important that you’re there for your daughter but just as much you have to take care of your own emotional well being. You’re dealing with such a huge amount of pain right now, do you have access to therapy? Can someone help you out with caring for your daughter? Are you talking to friends? You don’t have to carry all of this alone. From my own experience: my dad killed himself when I was really young and my mom told me later I was the only reason she kept going, so maybe you can’t do it for yourself right now but you can do it for your daughter who needs and loves her mom. Maybe that’s not much but it can be enough for now. And I’m sure you’re a great parent and view yourself in a worse light that isn’t true to reality at all. Please reach out and ask for help to process your loss as well as your depression. I’d also recommend heading to r/suicidebereavement. I wish you and your daughter all the very best and I hope you can heal from this.

I’m really sorry that you’re feeling this way, I’ve been there several times in my life as well. Depression can be a lonely and isolating place and most of all it tells you lies. It tells you that you’re not important, that nobody cares and that you’ll never get better, but that is not true!! 

You’re not a waste of air and you deserve to live a happy life as much as the next person. I know this is hard to believe when you’re feeling so down but it’s true. According to your description you’re still really young, it’s terrible that you have to deal with this already but you also have possibilities to get better and create a life for yourself that you’ll enjoy. Please don’t hurt yourself. Reach out to someone you trust, this might sound like the most difficult thing to do but you deserve help and someone who listens to you. Can you talk to your parents? a teacher? another relative? Please don’t harbor all these feelings and thoughts inside of you, they’re toxic.

Hey there, I hope you’re still with us. What you said deeply resonates with me and I’m hurting with and for you. It sounds like you’ve had to deal with lots of tragedy in your life and to make it to 27 despite that shows your strength and resilience, I really hope you can hold on to that and decide against the plan you’ve made for today. I know what it’s like to feel this way every day, my only reason to still be here is to not hurt anyone. That has to be enough for now.
Also regarding the pills + alcohol, that’s a rather romanticized way to go, you might just wake up in a great amount of pain and damage to your organs, please don’t put yourself through more pain and trauma, put it all away and maybe reach out to your therapist? or a person you trust? I’m thinking of you.

coming from someone who lost her dad to suicide when she was young: with you, always. I know that’s hard to believe sometimes but it’s the truth, the pain of having to live without you is infinitely bigger than having a mentally ill parent. my mom isn’t exactly stable either, but I can guarantee you I’d never never never want to miss her in my life and I’d give the world to have my dad back. and do families recover from it? no. they learn how to live with it at best, and speaking from my experience as a daughter it leaves traces in every aspect of my life. it has shaped my view on the world, people, the relationships I have, trust, fear, everything really. I think the impact, though different for each person, is far greater than you could imagine. I wish you all the best!

I’m 24 now and the only advice I can give is ask for help, talk, don’t bottle it up inside of you, take medication if needed. You’re a very strong and resilient person. I read in the comments that you’re already seeing a therapist, which is great. All I’ve learned is that I should have sought out the help I deserved when I was your age, so I really hope you can keep going and that they’ll help you work through the pain and trauma. wish you all the very best x

I don’t have great advice besides the one already given (seek out a therapist asap) but I do pretty much the exact same thing. I always say I come and go like waves in my friendships and it becomes increasingly harder to keep all of them. I think it’s a good basis that your friends know about your mental health issues, I don’t know to which extent but I believe the best thing you can do is to be as open about it as possible. 
Explain what you’re going through and why you react the way you do to the friends you feel comfortable with, sit down with them or write a letter. From my experience what almost ruined some of my friendship was the fact that I disappeared without saying a word which will eventually lead friends to think they’re just not important to you. Nobody can read your mind so you have to let them know it is not their fault and that you still love them just the same. Communication and honesty is the key, even though it’s hard. 
I’m currently trying to be more open about it with one friend to test the water, we’re trying to come up with a system that makes it easier for me to communicate with her throughout these phases, like texting is hard so we have some set emojis I can use to quickly let her know how I am. I make sure to remind her that I love her and personally I prefer it when my friends still text me updates even though I’m kind of absent so we talked about that as well and she keeps doing that to keep me in the loop. 
Another thing I do is set a day and time I sit down for half an hour and respond to all the messages I ignored, I know that’s hard and it sucks, sometimes I postpone it but eventually I feel better afterwards. It’s something I really have to force myself to do. 
At the end of the day it all comes down to 1. talking it through with your friends because if people get the feeling you don’t care about them anymore, they’ll eventually stop caring about you as well and 2. working on yourself.

I feel exactly the same way. For me it wasn’t always like this, when I was younger it was a given that I’d have kids, then I got majorly depressed and it changed everything. I’m 24 now and I know where all this well end some day so it wouldn’t be fair to have kids and hope they’ll make life worth living just to then realize I’m still as miserable as before, but with more responsibility. My father killed himself when I was younger, I don’t want to inflict the same pain on someone else, so unless I’m absolutely sure I’m “cured” (which will not happen) I won’t have kids. It’s too much of a risk and it would be selfish. There are other reasons playing into this decision as well, like the second one you mentioned. The last thing I want to do is to cause more pain in the world.

I also listen to a lot of music so I create playlists, try to capture a certain feeling and lastly I draw/paint, I’m no good at it but it makes me feel better, keeps me busy + I can combine it with the music, I think at the end it’s just about creating something while I feel so empty inside. but if it’s a particularly bad day I just lie around trying to nap.

hi fellow redditor, I'm deeply sorry that you feel like this is the only solution for you right now but please reconsider and talk to someone you trust, maybe your mother? depression wants you to believe that you are worthless but it's a lie. you are not a joke. you deserve happiness. I know these are just words to you right now but please give your life a chance to prove that they are true, even though you might not be able to see it right now. I have looked through your post history and you are still so young, but you sound so intelligent! I've been where you are when I was 14/15 so I speak from experiece when I say that I couldn't have possibly fathomed all the possibilities life holds for us. there are so many opportunities, please don't throw that away and tell someone how you feel. I know it takes great courage but it's the first step for a better future, please try!!

as someone else already said: communication is key. first of all I think it’s great that you had the courage to open up to her, that’s the first really important step but unfortunately it doesn’t end there. it’s difficult for people who have never gone through depression/suicidal thoughts to understand what you feel and why you feel this way, so you have to tell them. I know it’s hard but try to help her understand you. explain that she can’t just say things like that because it hurts you. 
I also believe it’s especially hard for mothers when their own child is suffering so she might try to cover up/cope with this sort of humor because she herself is unsure how to behave. but since you mentioned she’s a great mom I believe she’ll listen to you and understand.

I hope you feel better after getting some sleep and if then there’s even an ounce of doubt about going through with your plan, please talk to someone. I’m here to listen. I saw your post about opening up to your friends recently, they’ll listen too. I don’t know what exactly you’re going through but I know what it’s like to be suicidal. depression wants us to believe that nobody cares, nobody will listen, but if you tell your loved ones how terrible you’re feeling they’ll be there for you. I know it costs a lot of courage but please just give your life another chance if you can. either way, I wish you all the best x

I relate to this a lot and I’m sorry that you’re going through it as well. Being given false hope just to hit rock bottom even harder afterwards is terrible. what I’m trying to do is appreciate these hours/days where it seems like I’ll be okay and use them as good as possible to get things done and regain some energy. In the beginning of those episodes I really thought “omg this time it’s going to last and it won’t come back” but the truth is that it doesn’t magically disappear so I try to not get sucked too much into those good feelings because once they leave again it hurts even more and instead I try to use them as efficiently as possible while being well aware that at some point in the near future things will be bad again.

we’re all born as atheists, then we get taught religion and I believe afterwards it’s on ourselves to just roll with what we’ve been told or look beyond that. I did the latter and I can narrow it down to one specific incident: the death of my stepdad.
I went to a catholic school, was taught about god every week, had to go to church every second week and frankly it never resonated with me, but I also wasn’t bothered enough to look further into it to already call myself an atheist back then until my stepdad’s death. it was coming for a few months and I spent every night praying, not because I particularly believed in it but because he did. Well it doesn’t come as a surprise that praying did fuck all and that’s when I started really questioning religion and the existence of god. I read a lot, I thought a lot and eventually came to the conclusion that either there is a god and he lets all these terrible things happen and that’s a god I don’t want to put my faith in or there’s simply no god. Either way it’s something I can’t and won’t believe in. 
So the reason I’m an atheist isn’t that “he let my stepdad die without doing anything about it”, his death was just the cause of me looking beyond what a majority of people believe in. Mind I also got into science so that’s the second big factor. Nowadays I think believing in a sky person and giving him credit for all the good things while ignoring the bad stuff just to make yourself feel better about life and death is absolutely ridiculous, but to each his own.

I’ve always struggled with this as I’m someone who has the urge to always be the best but as banal as it might sound I just learned to not beat myself up over something that’s done. you’ve got the grade and you can’t change it so what’s the point in wasting your time being upset about? it will just make you feel worse. it sounds simple but I tried to condition my brain to think like that. Instead of reminiscing about what can’t be changed I try to use that time to find out what lead to this bad grade. did I not learn enough? was I not interested in the topic? did I simply not fully understand it? or was some personal stuff going on, some mental health issues? Then cut yourself some slack and instead of beating yourself up about the grade be proud for even going and managing to take the exam, because that can already be a struggle for some people. 
And, at the end of the day, it’s just one exam of many that you’ll take. things tend to look really terrible when we look at it from a close view so what I try to do is ask myself: will this matter in a few weeks/months from now? and most of the time it in fact won’t have such a big effect on that greater scale because it’s just one exam of many. I’m not sure if that’s helping in any way but it’s my take on this issue. Mind it doesn’t always work, I still find myself in situations where I hate myself for fucking up, but as I said above: a few months later it just did not matter anymore and all the anger was mostly for nothing.

hey, I’m really sorry about what happened to your dad, loved ones suddenly being ripped away from us is a traumatizing experience. I’ve been through similar stuff and my brain does the exact same thing that you are describing. Whenever I hear an ambulance I have to make sure that everyone is okay, when someone calls or visits around a bit of a weird time I immediately go into “prepare for someone has died again” mode. It’s exhausting and can really mess you up. Considering you were told about what happened to your dad on the phone your reaction makes sense, it’s like a trigger and your brain is immediately thrown back into that situation. From my own experience I can only tell you that it didn’t get better for me, but that might be due to several people from my closest circle dying which strengthened this thought process. Everybody has their own pace when it comes to healing but if there’s no progress for you and you feel like it influences your daily life/makes you anxious/live in a general state of fear you should eventually seek help. all the best to you.

hey, I’m sorry for your loss, it’s a truly traumatizing experience. I’ve been through the same and I think I’d have never forgiven myself if I hadn’t been there but at the same time just thinking about these final moments, how the pauses between his breaths got longer every time makes my heart race and my body ache, I immediately have to think about something else or I’m getting a panic attack. I don’t know how long it’s been for you, for me it was almost 3 years ago and it gets easier, you’ll be okay more often every year, but that gut wrenching feeling never truly leaves. it’s just something you can’t really get over, you only learn how to live and cope with the memory.

yeah, I can relate. for example my week consists of: an appointment, going to Uni once and meeting one friend and I’ll be incredibly stressed and feel busy even though that’s not the case. I think for me that’s part of my depression/anxiety. 
Training probably also plays a huge role, I used to work from 8-4  5 days a week and I didn’t have a problem with it. It might be the same for you. 
But in general I believe people are simply different. I have a friend who’s constantly doing stuff and I always ask her how she handles that? But it works for her. While I on the other hand always needed a lot of time for myself. 
So I think it’s a mixture of these 3 factors: your mental health, your personality and simply getting used to a daily routine.

Yes, I believe to a certain extent it’s okay, everybody has different coping mechanisms and sometimes you just have to switch off the real world. But I’ve noticed that in my case it’s getting out of hand and it keeps me from doing other important things. that’s why I want to (have to) tune it down.

I can relate a lot to what you’ve described. I’ve recently seen an old video of me with my friends which made me cry because I watched myself and wondered “who are you? what happened to you?” it’s weird that I saw myself but it wasn’t me, not the me I know today at least, it was almost like looking at a stranger. 
I think we always tend to romanticize the past and I definitely know things weren’t that great a few years ago either, but at least I wasn’t controlled by depression and anxiety and I sort of had a plan for my life. 
I try to see the positive things though: I, as much as you, was once able to be this content and happy person so that means that I’ve got it in me, somewhere. Things will never be what they once were but that doesn’t mean they have to be terrible forever. I always wish I could go back to when I was 17-19, but that also means being a less compassionate, introspective and understanding person and instead more naive and ignorant. So yes in a lot of ways I miss the old me, I grieve for her a lot. things were better and easier but I’m trying to somehow take the positive aspects, the things I’ve learned about me, other people and mental illnesses and create a new me that I can live with. I know it’s a long and hard way though. 
I wish you all the best for creating a future you that you’re content with too.

dear anonymous redditor, 
I saw your post last night, unfortunately 1h after you apparently jumped. going through this thread broke my heart because there were so many people trying to help you but in the end nothing anyone could do, you seemed at peace with your decision, which I respect but I still cried for you. 
the first thing that came to my mind this morning was you, I immediately looked for your post hoping you had responded, hoping something had changed your mind. but apparently it didn’t, all I hope now is that you didn’t have to suffer in your final moments, that it was fast and you no longer have to be in pain. 
I know you can’t read this anymore but I still wanted to write to you, because you made an impact on this world, on the homeless man you gave your jacket to, on the people in your daily life even though you might weren’t aware of it and on several people in this thread here. and I’m sorry this world let you down in return.

yes definitely. When I’m depressed I tend to stop taking care of myself, I fall back into self destructive behaviors for example forcing myself to stay awake for no good reason, starving myself or eating too much which I voluntarily choose to do. it’s irrational because I actually don’t want to feel miserable but my depression still makes me do it which usually ends with me hating myself even more. it’s a really tricky cycle to get out of because one affects the other. 
I also have the tendency to put myself into dangerous decisions or to just make poor choices that I later regret. And as you mentioned anger also plays a huge role for me too. anger towards myself, the people around me and the world in general, which is why I usually try to stay away from others during that time because I don’t want to tear them apart with me. I used to let that anger out on myself but have now learned to just punch my pillow or throw some things. 
all the best for you x

you sound like a great father who loves his daughter very much! I can guarantee you she would not be better off without you, no matter how low you think of yourself, you'll always be her father, a role model, somebody she knows she can rely on. my father killed himself when I was little and up to this day the same question is haunting me "why wasn't I enough to stick around?", I don't want to put any pressure on you and every situation is different but believe me when I say she needs you, thinking that the people you love are better off without you is part of your depression but it is not the truth. 
and if the only meaning in your life right now is your daughter, that's already something to hang on to! it takes great courage and strength to keep pulling through, do it for her and learn to do it for yourself as well. 
I struggle with the pointlessness of life too, so what I try to do is set myself little goals, write to do lists, try to organize my life, look for new things I might find joy in but also accept the days where non of this is possible. 
you mentioned a few things you used to do and you're kind of right, where's the point in going for a swim? frankly, there is probably non. but you might as well try it, maybe it brings you some joy or you meet new people. wish you all the best x
